title: Fall Bridge: Strategy Reset & Ops Tactical
summary: Quarterly-ish reset to align on product priorities, capacity planning, hiring cadence, and a short ops deep-dive on latency incidents + remedial playbooks. Emphasis on tying cost controls to SLA commitments and a clear set of next steps for leader owners.
action_items: Markus Jensen - Publish trimmed incident postmortem and remediation timeline by 2026-09-10
Lena Ortiz - Update product roadmap priorities and share trimmed feature list for Q4 by 2026-09-12
Jonas Meyer - Rework pricing communication for Dedicated to sales deck by 2026-09-11
Priya Patel - Circulate hiring hold exceptions policy and manager checklist by 2026-09-09
Ava Li - Run two structured canary runs for the new KV cache config next week and report metrics
next_steps: Leadership to review trimmed roadmap doc and OKR adjustments (owners: Samir, Lena, Markus)
Schedule technical deep-dive on latency optimizations w/ serving team (invite SEs + infra)
Share incident postmortem and link to runbooks in #incidents channel
Townhall recording and slide deck to be posted to Notion
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-07
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samir Rao (CEO), Emily Chen (CTO), Lena Ortiz (VP Product), Markus Jensen (Head of Eng), Priya Patel (Head of People), Jonas Meyer (Head of Revenue), Ava Li (Head of Reliability), company-wide audience (~120)

[00:00] Samir: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for making time. We're going to keep it tight - 50-ish minutes - focus on ops, the incident recap, and then a short strategy pivot for the fall quarter. Quick note, recording is on.

[00:24] Emily: Hi all. I'll start with a brief of what happened last week — the latency spike tied to the KV cache eviction path. Short version: we saw repeated cold-start flows when the new quantized model variant was routed under burst. There was a shader/kernel mismatch on a subset of nodes, which produced extended decode times.

[00:49] Markus: Right. To add, the auto-balance logic pushed load to older instances that didn't have the optimized kernels. There was also an edge case in the allocator when sequences exceeded 2K tokens. That was missed in the smoke tests.

[01:12] Speaker 1: (inaudible) — I thought the canary had covered that?

[01:18] Emily: We did a canary but it wasn't representative — the seq length distribution in canary was narrower. We need better workload-sim canaries.

[01:35] Samir: Okay, go ahead and walk through the mitigation timeline and what's next.

[01:40] Markus: Mitigation chronology: 1) routing fallback to the stable model variant; 2) hotfix to the kernel selection in the allocator; 3) temporarily disabled the aggressive autoscale burst policy; 4) rolling update of nodes with the corrected kernel. From detection to rollback was ~7.5 minutes, and full stabilization took about 43 minutes.

[02:10] Ava: Observability gaps: we didn't have a token-level latency heatmap for the burst lane. We had traces but they were filtered by service name and we lost the cross-cut correlation.

[02:29] Samir: Ok that's a gap to close this week. Also, can we put a guardrail on auto-burst changes? Jonas: pricing/comms question — how did customers see it?

[02:45] Jonas: A handful of enterprise customers saw transient errors on P0 routes, filed tickets, CSMs escalated. We didn't hit SLA thresholds but customer confidence dipped. We should be proactive. I'm drafting a note to impacted customers that explains cause + corrective actions.

[03:05] Priya: Also worth noting incident stress on on-call — people are tired. If we're tightening the deployment cadence we should also adjust on-call rotations, at least temporarily.

[03:18] Samir: Agreed. Priya, work with infra leads to propose short-term rotation adjustments.

[03:25] Lena: Moving to product priorities — given the incident and cost push, I'm proposing we de-scope three lower-impact features slated for Q4 and move that effort into reliability and performance. We have to prioritize unit economics controls: batching defaults, quantization profiles, and cache TTL tuning.

[03:50] Emily: On batching and quantization: we have evidence that enabling default dynamic batching for interactive routes reduces cost per token by 18% at 95th percentile latency impact of ~40ms if we tune windowing. But that 40ms can be material for some low-latency customers. So we need per-route policy gating.

[04:16] Samir: So product should produce a per-route policy matrix?

[04:20] Lena: Yes. I'll publish a matrix that maps customer classes to defaults and recommended guardrails.

[04:27] Jonas: Sales and RevOps need a clear messaging pack for Dedicated and Hosted differences — specifically around burst behaviour, reserved capacity SLAs, and fallbacks. Customers ask: if we move to Dedicated, do we get absolute isolation? The answer is "near-isolation + routing fallbacks" — we need crisp language.

[04:50] Samir: Competitors are shouting full isolation — BigCloudAI claims hardware isolation guarantees. We need to be clearer on economic tradeoffs.

[05:01] Emily: Actionable items on tech: 1) improved workload-sim canaries; 2) per-node kernel ver checks in pre-deploy; 3) token-level latency dashboards for burst lanes.

[05:18] Markus: I'll take the kernel ver checks and coordinate with infra ops for a preflight.

[05:22] Ava: I'll own the token-level dashboards and canary tuning. Need help from SREs.

[05:30] Audience: (applause, muffled)

[05:41] Samir: Ok, hiring and budget. We had previously said hiring continues but with this mid-quarter reassessment, leadership recommends a temporary hiring pause for IC roles except critical infra/product gaps. Priya will issue guidelines.

[06:00] Priya: The guidance: immediate freeze on non-critical requisitions; exceptions require a one-pager justification and leadership sign-off. Managers should re-evaluate ongoing interviews and prioritize internal mobility.

[06:18] Lena: We'll also take two contractors' budget to fund short infra catch-up work for 3 months.

[06:28] Jonas: On GTM, I'm proposing an accelerated campaign for Dedicated showing cost math and predictable latency. Also add a health-check offering: free pilot with a latency/cost audit for top 10 strategic accounts.

[06:45] Samir: Good. Keep it tight and measurable. Jonas, deliver the pilot scope by Friday.

[07:00] Jonas: Yep.

[07:05] Audience Q&A

[07:12] Employee (X): Quick question — what's the timeline for the trimmed roadmap and the public-facing messaging?

[07:20] Lena: Trimmed roadmap to be shared within 5 working days. Public comms after we align on the message and the pricing deck — target next Wednesday.

[07:35] Employee (Y): Will there be any changes to the on-call compensation or backfill for people pulled into incident?

[07:42] Priya: We will propose increased incident pay for those on the escalation roster this month and fast-track temporary backfills. Details in the HR bulletin.

[08:00] Samir: Let's do a quick readout of OKR impacts — who sees the biggest delta?

[08:06] Lena: Product OKR adjusting: reliability +2 priority, new features -3 priority buckets; will update the OKR doc.

[08:18] Emily: Tech OKRs: add a new metric for 95th percentile token latency on burst lanes; target 15% improvement by end of Q4.

[08:30] Markus: Engineering will re-prioritize sprints for the next two cycles to push kernel and canary work.

[08:40] Samir: Cool. Final topic — compliance and audits. We have a SOC 2 readiness run next month. Any blockers?

[08:50] Ava: We have two outstanding items: encryption key rotation policy automation and audit logging retention policy for private deploys. Both are on-track but need product sign-off for retention defaults.

[09:05] Lena: Product is fine with a 90-day default for hosted logs and a configurable retention for Private customers. We'll document the defaults.

[09:18] Samir: Perfect. Quick recap of decisions and owners before we close.

[09:25] Samir: 1) Hiring pause with exceptions - owner Priya. 2) Incident postmortem + remediation timeline - owner Markus. 3) Token-level dashboards + canaries - owner Ava. 4) Trimmed roadmap - owner Lena. 5) Pricing and Dedicated messaging - owner Jonas. 6) SOC2 readiness follow ups - owner Ava/Lena.

[09:45] Emily: I'll follow up with the infra team about the pre-deploy kernel ver check and run a test in staging by EoW.

[09:52] Samir: Great. Thanks, everyone. Recording and slides will be posted. If you have more questions drop them in #all-hands-questions.

[10:00] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: There are short gaps where speaker turns overlap; a few technical terms may be slightly mangled ("KV cache" sometimes appears as "K V cache"; model names redacted in transcript). Some audience comments are summarized.
